info.title: API.SH: timeanddate
info.description: The timeanddate API from API.SH: public timeanddate data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

tags.description: Your balance, usage, logs and past responses. Free.

get.summary: Fetch a past response again, free

get.description:
Every country with a holiday list on timeanddate.com, with the slug to use in /timeanddate/v1/holidays.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/timeanddate-holiday-countries

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Public holidays and observances by country
get.description:
Public holidays and observances for a country and year: date, weekday, name, type (national, state/local, observance, religious, season, clock change, UN day...), where it applies and its page link. Filter by category.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/timeanddate-holidays

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: timeanddate country slug (us, uk, germany, india...; see /timeanddate/v1/holiday-countries).

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Categories, comma-separated: national, local, local_observance, important_observance, common_observance, other_observance, season, clock_change, worldwide, united_nations, christian, christian_more, jewish, jewish_more, muslim, hindu, orthodox, sport.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.title: Holidays and Observances in the United States in 2026

get.summary: Moonrise and moonset table for a month
get.description:
Moonrise and moonset with direction, a second moonrise where one falls on the same day, meridian passing time and altitude, Earth-Moon distance, illumination and the moon phases (with time) for every day of a month in one place.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/timeanddate-moon

parameters.name: place
parameters.description: timeanddate place path (e.g. usa/new-york) or a place link.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.name: New York, New York, USA — Moonrise, Moonset, and Moon Phases, December 2026

get.description:
Finds cities and places on timeanddate.com by name, with the place path to use in the other timeanddate endpoints, region, country, country code and popularity.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/timeanddate-search

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

items.name: Parish Saint Catherine / Saint Catherine (first-order administrative division)

get.summary: Sunrise and sunset table for a month
get.description:
Sunrise and sunset with direction, day length and its change, astronomical, nautical and civil twilight, solar noon with the sun's altitude and the Earth-Sun distance for every day of a month in one place (24-hour local time; nulls where the sun does not rise or set).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/timeanddate-sun

parameters.name: place
parameters.description: timeanddate place path (e.g. uk/london) or a place link.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.name: London, England, United Kingdom — Sunrise, Sunset, and Daylength, June 2027
notes: * All times are local time for London. Time is adjusted for DST when applicable. They take into account refraction . Dates are based on the …

get.summary: Current local time in a place
get.description:
Current local time and date in a city with its time zone (abbreviation, name, UTC offset), this year's daylight saving changes, location facts (country, state, coordinates, elevation, currency, languages, dialing code), today's sunrise, sunset, day length, solar noon and twilights, moonrise, moonset, illumination and phases, and tide times where the site lists them.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/timeanddate-time

parameters.name: place
parameters.description: timeanddate place path (e.g. usa/new-york, uk/london, @2988507) or a timeanddate.com place link.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Or a place name (the best match is used).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Time zone and clock changes for a place
get.description:
A place's current time zone, next change and UTC offset, and every clock change (daylight saving start and end, zone changes) for a decade: date and time, abbreviation and name before and after, the change and the offset after. `start_year` picks the decade (back to 1800s).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/timeanddate-timezone

parameters.name: place
parameters.description: timeanddate place path (e.g. usa/new-york) or a place link.

parameters.name: start_year
parameters.description: A year in the decade to list (YYYY; default the current years).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Every time zone abbreviation with its full name, alternative names, where it is used and its UTC offset; `q` filters by abbreviation, name or location.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/timeanddate-timezone-abbreviations

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Filter text, e.g. EST or Australia.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
